text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HET FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Bank-insurer Fortis merges stock-broking units KBW and Wesselius. A third, Theodoor Gilissen, will continue to operate independently, under aegis of Fortis's MeesPierson. (p1)
- Government must help small and medium-sized companies with information technology. (p3)
- Transport concern Nedlloyd sells its subsidiary Geytenbeek to Marcon Nederland. (p4)
- Internet service provider Videotex plans a bourse launch in two years to finance expansion. (p4)
- Dutch Rail NS is to get new competiton from three companies. (p3)
DE VOLKSKRANT
- Higher dollar will boost earnings of large Dutch companies with subsidiaries in the U.S. (p1)
- ABN Amro Bank places large order with information technology company Oracle. (p2)
- Insurer Aegon is prepared to reach financial settlement with surviving relatives of Jewish policy-holders who perished in World War Two. (p3)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Unemployment in Amsterdam area falls sharply in one year's time. (p1)
- Real estate fund Uni-Invest seeks to take over Capa City. (p19)
- Investors' lobby group VEB warns of hysteria generated by stock exchange flotations. (p19)
TROUW
- Transport minister Annemarie Jorritsma allows PTT Telecom to go ahead with offer of free voice mail to subscribers. (p19)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- ICI factory at Rozenburg near Rotterdam will be transferred from ICI to DuPont under a broader deal between the two companies. (p11)
